I don't know where else to post this, so I'll share it here and let the community spread it out.

So anyway there's this extension for Firefox (and Chrome) called HTTPS Everywhere. The purpose of the extension is to force sites that provide HTTPS access to use that exclusively. It comes with a bunch of built-in rulesets, but there's no ruleset for Voat built-in.

If you're using HTTPS Everywhere on Firefox, you can add support fairly easily.

  1. Open up the HTTPSEverywhereUserRules folder inside your Firefox profile (Will be somewhere like C:\Users\{username}\AppData\Roaming\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\{blahblahblah}.default)
  2. Create a new file in that folder called voat.xml
  3. Copy the contents of this paste into voat.xml
  4. Restart Firefox
  5. Go to voat.co
  6. Click on the HTTPS Everywhere button and ensure that the "voat" item on the menu that appears is checked

There you go, HTTPS-only access to Voat, all the time, without any further effort!
